subject: Geo-fencing archival & certified purge: questions and proposed language
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@citrinehealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Citrine Health Legal <legal@citrinehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Questions on archival guarantees and certified purge language

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for sending the draft DPA. Our legal team is primarily concerned about two operational guarantees before we can sign: 1) a clear certified purge process for deleted customer data (we need a signed attestation on request), and 2) how you handle short-lived diagnostic snapshots that may be copied across zones for debugging.

Specifically: can Redwood provide a certified purge certificate that includes a timestamp, scope (resources deleted), and signing authority? Also, is there an operational TTL for ephemeral snapshots used for live troubleshooting, and can Citrine opt-out of snapshots being copied outside the EU region?

I've attached our redlines (attachment: citrine_redline_comments.docx). Happy to hop on a quick call this week.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Compliance, Citrine Health
elena.morales@citrinehealth.com
+44 20 5555 1234

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@citrinehealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 11:08:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Questions on archival guarantees and certified purge language

Hi Elena,

Appreciate the fast review and the redlines — I uploaded them and skimmed the top items. Short answers up front: yes, we can provide a certified purge attestation on request; yes, you can restrict snapshots to EU-only copies via a geofencing flag in your account; and yes, we have an internal TTL for ephemeral debug snapshots (default 48 hours).

I'll lay out the proposed contractual language tweaks below and attach a draft attestation template for your legal team's review (attachment: redwood_dpa_certified_purge_draft.pdf).

Proposed contract edits (high level):
- Certified Purge Attestation: Redwood will provide a signed attestation within 10 business days of a verified erase request. Attestation will include deletion timestamp(s), list of logical resource identifiers (tenant id, snapshot ids), and the name/title of the signatory.
- Snapshot handling: add an opt-out clause allowing the customer to prevent cross-region snapshot replication; by default debug snapshots are ephemeral and TTL-limited.
- Archival exception: retain copy for regulatory audit only when a documented legal hold is provided; otherwise archival copies are subject to the same deletion SLA.

Next steps: Jonas and Marcus — can you confirm operational feasibility of 10 business days for attestation and whether signature will be automated (signed by Redwood Legal) vs manual? Laura — can you confirm the default TTLs and whether we can expose the geofence toggle in the Console before contract signature?

Naomi
Product Counsel, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
(attachment: redwood_dpa_certified_purge_draft.pdf)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Sep 2026 13:04:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Questions on archival guarantees and certified purge language

Naomi — quick operational confirmation.

- Certified purge attestation: feasible within 10 business days. We currently have an internal workflow that compiles deletion logs and artifacts; turning that into a formal PDF attestation is a 1-2 day addition to the workflow, but the full verification (cross-checking backups, snapshot indexes) is the slowest step.
- Signing: Redwood Legal will sign; we can automate generation but legal will need to sign or approve the template. For now we should say "signed by Redwood Legal or an authorized officer."
- Ephemeral snapshots: default TTL is 48 hours; we can offer a console toggle to set a policy per-tenant. Preventing cross-region copies is supported at the routing layer — we'll expose the flag and a policy that prevents replication during snapshot creation.

Caveat: For customers that opt into cross-region DR (disaster recovery), routing constraints may require an exception; we'll add a clause describing that DR opt-in supersedes the geofence unless customer explicitly maintains a geofence carve-out in writing.

Jonas
Director, Platform Reliability
jonas.weber@redwood.com

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@citrinehealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Citrine Health Legal <legal@citrinehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 10:22:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Questions on archival guarantees and certified purge language

Thanks Naomi and team — this helps. A few follow-ups from our legal counsel after reviewing your attestation template:

1) Scope granularity: they want the attestation to include hash digests for the deleted artifacts where technically feasible (so they can correlate with their internal logs). Is including SHA256 digests for snapshot objects practical?

2) Backup windows: they asked for an explicit statement that backups outside the active retention window will not be retained beyond the agreed deletion SLA; i.e., if TTL is 48 hours, no backups will be kept longer than that, except for legally required holds.

3) Audit trail: can Redwood expose an exportable, machine-readable deletion log (JSON/CSV) with timestamps, object ids, and processing status for the lifecycle event? They want to ingest it into their GRC tooling.

Legal offered a few suggested edits to the attestation template — attached (attachment: citrine_redline_comments.docx). We can schedule a 30-minute call Fri morning if useful.

Best,
Elena

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@citrinehealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 16:45:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Questions on archival guarantees and certified purge language

Elena — quick reply after checking with infra and product.

1) SHA256 digests: feasible for snapshots and stored artifacts created by Redwood. For streamed/ephemeral fragments that are never materialized as objects, we cannot produce digests; we'll document which artifacts are digestible. We'll add a sentence to the attestation template: "Where applicable, Redwood will include SHA256 digests for deleted artifacts."

2) Backup windows: we can commit to alignment between snapshot TTL and backup retention for customer-managed snapshots that are not under legal hold. We'll add a carve-out: backups that are part of customer-certified DR (explicit opt-in) may follow a different SLA and will be highlighted in the contract.

3) Machine-readable deletion log: yes — we'll provide a downloadable JSON export with fields (timestamp, object_id, snapshot_id, action, result, operator_id). We'll surface an S3/secure-URL export that Citrine Legal can pull. Note: for security we will redact internal operator identifiers and provide pseudonymous operator tokens — is that acceptable?

If these items are agreeable, Naomi/Richard from Legal can incorporate the text. Happy to join the call on Friday.

Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
